julie_sales: Heads-up 10AM PT kick for Lyra tomorrow. They asked for presales guidance: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering for our Private deployment POC, a minimal firewall allowlist they can give NetOps, and any pricing callouts. Can we put together a short checklist?

devon_netops: TL;DR: both valid. Quick tradeoffs: peering = simple L3 route (good for single-account or trusted cross-account VPCs). PrivateLink = interface endpoints, no route-table changes, better isolation and less blast radius. If they use TGW with many spokes, peering can get messy; PrivateLink requires an endpoint per spoke unless they use shared services pattern.

ana_security: (typo) ana_security: Security notes: PrivateLink reduces exposure by keeping traffic off the public internet and limiting to ENI IPs. But ensure that the customers egress firewall allows TLS to our service FQDN or the ENI CIDRs. For compliance: ask if they require logs to remain in their account; we can forward metrics but control-plane logs live in Redwood unless they opt for metrics-forwarding.

tom_se: Pricing bullets to flag to the customer: PrivateLink = per-interface endpoint hourly charge + GB processing fees on AWS. VPC peering = no endpoint hourly fee but watch inter-AZ/inter-region data transfer rates and cross-account egress costs. For a short POC, peering is often lower ops time/cost. For enterprise steady-state, PrivateLink is commonly preferred.

julie_sales: Can you give a copy-paste firewall allowlist and a single command they can run from their spoke VPC? They want to hand this to their netops.
devon_netops: Minimal allowlist (give to NetOps):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: redwood-lyra.private.redwood.example (FQDN)
- If firewall requires IPs: allow our egress CIDR 52.17.0.0/16 (sample) for hosted endpoints. Note: CIDR can change; prefer FQDN/DNS allowlist.
- For PrivateLink: allow ENI IP ranges in their VPC (no public IP required) and allow DNS resolution of the endpoint name.
- For VPC Peering: ensure route tables include the peer and NACLs/Security Groups allow ephemeral ports for TLS (1024-65535) if SGs are narrow.

devon_netops: Quick connectivity sanity test (run from a linux host in the spoke):
```
# resolve and https GET health endpoint (replace token)
curl -v -s -o /dev/null "https://redwood-lyra.private.redwood.example/v1/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood-poc-token"
```

devon_netops: If curl fails: traceroute/tcpdump suggestions:
- traceroute -T -p 443 <resolved-ip>
- sudo tcpdump -n -i any host <resolved-ip> and port 443 and capture SYN/ACK/RST
- Save pcap and share (we can interpret).

ana_security: For the security questionnaire blurb: we recommend PrivateLink for regulated workloads: no public IPs, per-VPC interface endpoints, supports security group controls on ENIs, and reduces need to change route tables. For peering, include that peered VPCs are L3-routed and you must control route propagation.

tom_se: SE checklist to include in the POC email to Lyra:
- Chosen connectivity: PrivateLink or Peering (state preferred)
- AWS account IDs / VPC IDs (for peering) or account + VPC for endpoint service acceptance (for PrivateLink)
- Who will accept endpoint connection (IAM principal)
- Test window: we propose 2026-04-02 09:00-11:00 PT (SE on-call)
- Expected QPS / concurrency so we can suggest Hosted vs Dedicated for POC sizing and cost ranges

julie_sales: What about static egress IPs? Lyra wants a single outbound IP in their firewall policy if possible.
devon_netops: Hosted endpoints: not guaranteed single static public IP; we recommend DNS-based allowlist. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provision a NAT + Elastic IPs for stable outbound addresses, but that is extra engineering and may be a paid optional network addon. Mention as a potential blocker in the deal if they insist on immutable public IPs for hosted.

tom_se: Also remind them: PrivateLink requires acceptance if the endpoint service is cross-account. We'll need the endpoint connection request and an admin in our account to accept. Provide the docs link in the email.

ops-deploy-bot: NOTE: tentative test window scheduled: 2026-04-02 09:00-11:00 PT. Reply with participant list to lock.

julie_sales: I'll include vendops@lyra.com in the invite and ask for NetOps contact. Action items:
- @tom_se: draft POC email + rough cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated & callout PrivateLink hourly/GB estimate by EOD.
- @devon_netops: paste the allowlist and tcpdump/traceroute snippets into the email and add a short TGW note about per-spoke endpoints.
- @ana_security: 1-paragraph answer for their security questionnaire about PrivateLink vs peering.

tom_se: Will do. One more enterprise note: if Lyra wants audit logs in their account, we can arrange metrics/event forwarding; full control-plane logs require Private deployment and additional config. Flag that in the email.

julie_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll send the mail once tom posts the draft. :thumbsup:
